variants.title: VASCULAR DUPLEX ULTRASOUND — ARTERIOVENOUS MALFORMATION (AVM) (NORMAL STUDY)

blocks.x: Intermittent throbbing sensation in the left volar forearm; rule out arteriovenous malformation.

High-frequency linear (7.5–15 MHz) and curvilinear (3–5 MHz) gray-scale, color Doppler, and pulsed-wave spectral Doppler sonography performed over the region of interest and adjacent major inflow/outflow vessels.
Lesion Morphology: No vascular malformation. Normal subcutaneous adipose tissue and homogeneous skeletal muscle architecture, without tortuous vascular channels or solid soft-tissue mass.
Dimensions & Depth: Not applicable (no lesion identified).
Vascular Density: No abnormal hypervascularity or turbulent mosaic aliasing on color Doppler.
Feeding Arteries: The radial and ulnar arteries demonstrate normal caliber and normal high-resistance triphasic spectral waveforms, without abnormal low-resistance shunting.
Draining Veins: The paired radial, ulnar, and superficial cephalic/basilic veins are patent and compressible with normal phasic venous flow and no arterialization.
Adjacent Major Artery & Deep Veins: Patent; no deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or signs of distal arterial steal phenomenon.
Underlying Bone / Nerve: Smooth cortical margin of underlying bone; no acute hematoma or abscess.
Normal soft tissue and vascular duplex ultrasound of the left volar forearm; no sonographic evidence of an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) or vascular anomaly.

bank_title: VASCULAR DUPLEX ULTRASOUND — ARTERIOVENOUS MALFORMATION (AVM) — PHRASES BANK

bank.title: 1. Negative Study (Normal Soft Tissue — No Vascular Malformation)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Intermittent throbbing sensation in the left volar forearm; rule out arteriovenous malformation.

subs.title: Findings
items: High-frequency gray-scale and color/spectral Doppler interrogation of the left volar forearm demonstrates normal subcutaneous adipose tissue and normal homogeneous skeletal muscle architecture without tortuous vascular channels, abnormal hypervascularity, or solid soft tissue mass.
The radial and ulnar arteries demonstrate normal caliber and normal high-resistance triphasic spectral waveforms without abnormal low-resistance shunting.
The paired radial, ulnar, and superficial cephalic/basilic veins are patent and compressible with normal phasic venous flow and no arterialization.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal soft tissue and vascular duplex ultrasound of the left volar forearm; no sonographic evidence of an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) or vascular anomaly.

bank.title: 2. Classic Congenital High-Flow Soft Tissue AVM (Subcutaneous / Intramuscular)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Warm, pulsatile soft tissue swelling in the medial right thigh with an audible bruit and skin erythema (Schobinger Stage II).

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the subcutaneous tissue and extending into the superficial vastus medialis muscle of the medial right thigh, there is a poorly marginated, non-mass-forming cluster (nidus) of tortuous, dilated anechoic vascular channels measuring 4.6 x 2.3 x 3.8 cm without a discrete solid soft-tissue mass.
Color Doppler reveals dense, turbulent mosaic aliasing throughout the nidus.

Spectral Doppler demonstrates multiple hypertrophied feeding arterial branches arising from the right superficial femoral artery exhibiting markedly elevated velocities (PSV = 165 cm/s, EDV = 98 cm/s) and abnormally low-resistance waveforms (RI = 0.40).
Multiple dilated draining veins empty into the great saphenous vein and demonstrate turbulent, pulsatile arterialized venous waveforms (PSV = 75 cm/s).

subs.title: Impression
items: High-flow arteriovenous malformation (AVM) of the medial right thigh (4.6 cm nidus) involving the subcutaneous and superficial intramuscular compartments, fed by branches of the right superficial femoral artery and draining into the great saphenous venous system.
Contrast-enhanced MRA/CTA and multidisciplinary vascular anomalies / interventional radiology consultation recommended for mapping and embolization planning.

bank.title: 3. Acquired / Post-Traumatic AVM (Cirsoid Aneurysm of the Scalp / Face)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Enlarging, pulsatile, tortuous mass over the right temporal scalp 1 year after blunt/penetrating scalp laceration.

subs.title: Findings
items: Centered within the subcutaneous layer of the right temporal scalp is a dense, serpiginous tangle of markedly dilated, tortuous vascular channels measuring 3.4 x 1.2 x 2.8 cm without an intervening solid mass.

Color and spectral Doppler confirm direct high-velocity arteriovenous shunting fed by a markedly dilated right superficial temporal artery (PSV = 190 cm/s, RI = 0.38) and draining into dilated, arterialized superficial temporal and scalp veins (PSV = 85 cm/s).
The underlying outer table of the calvarium is smooth and intact.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acquired high-flow arteriovenous malformation (cirsoid aneurysm) of the right temporal scalp (3.4 cm), supplied by the right superficial temporal artery.
CTA of the head/neck and interventional neuroradiology consultation advised prior to endovascular or surgical treatment.

bank.title: 4. Intramuscular AVM with Distal Arterial Steal Phenomenon

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Painful swelling in the left calf with exercise-induced claudication and cool distal foot.

subs.title: Findings
items: Infiltrating the medial head of the left gastrocnemius muscle is an extensive high-flow AVM nidus measuring 5.8 x 3.1 x 4.5 cm composed of multiple dilated, tortuous intramuscular vessels without a discrete solid tumor mass.

Feeding branches from the left posterior tibial and peroneal arteries demonstrate high-velocity, low-resistance monophasic flow (PSV = 210 cm/s, RI = 0.35), draining into dilated arterialized gastrocnemius and posterior tibial veins.

Distal to the AVM, the left posterior tibial artery at the ankle demonstrates markedly dampened, low-velocity monophasic waveforms (PSV = 22 cm/s) compared to the normal triphasic right posterior tibial artery (PSV = 68 cm/s), consistent with distal arterial steal.

subs.title: Impression
items: Extensive intramuscular high-flow arteriovenous malformation (5.8 cm) within the left medial gastrocnemius muscle, fed by posterior tibial and peroneal arterial branches.
Hemodynamic evidence of distal arterial steal phenomenon affecting the left posterior tibial artery at the ankle. Urgent vascular / interventional radiology referral recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Follow-up ultrasound 4 weeks after transarterial embolization of a left forearm AVM.

subs.title: Findings
items: Compared to the pre-procedural baseline study, approximately 75% of the previously documented 3.5 cm AVM nidus in the proximal left forearm is now obliterated by non-compressible echogenic thrombus and bright echogenic embolic material with posterior acoustic shadowing.

A small residual 1.1 x 0.7 cm focus of persistent turbulent color Doppler flow remains at the deep medial aspect of the nidus, fed by a small branch of the left ulnar artery demonstrating mildly elevated diastolic flow (PSV = 95 cm/s, RI = 0.54).
The main radial and ulnar arteries remain widely patent with normal distal waveforms.

subs.title: Impression
items: Interval partial thrombosis/obliteration (~75%) of the left forearm AVM following embolization, with a small residual 1.1 cm perfused nidus component fed by an ulnar artery branch.

bank.title: 6. Key Differential Mimic — Low-Flow Venous Malformation (VM) (To Rule Out AVM)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Soft, bluish compressible mass in the left cheek that enlarges when crying or bending forward; evaluate for AVM vs. venous malformation.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the buccal subcutaneous tissue of the left cheek, there is a well-marginated, lobulated, sponge-like collection of compressible, dilated anechoic sinusoidal vascular spaces measuring 2.9 x 1.5 x 2.2 cm containing two small punctate echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing (phleboliths).

Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate slow, sluggish monophasic venous flow only during probe release/Valsalva maneuver, with complete absence of high-velocity arterialized waveforms, feeding arterial hypertrophy, or arteriovenous shunting.

subs.title: Impression
items: Low-flow venous malformation (VM) of the left cheek (2.9 cm) containing characteristic phleboliths.
No evidence of high-flow arteriovenous malformation (AVM) or arteriovenous shunting; suitable for percutaneous sclerotherapy evaluation.
